To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

macrophage scavenger receptors (SR), which mediate endocytic clearance of extracellular material, also control the secretory repertoire by shuttling newly synthesized proteins to lysosomal secretory compartment.
stabilin-1, an endocytic receptor, controls the release of SI-CLP and other stabilin-1 ligands by the regulated secretory pathway.
stabilin-1, a scavenger receptor, is a unique endocytic receptor that links endocytosis and lysosomal secretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of novel receptors that are involved in the clearance of endogenous and exogenous material, in particular in the clearance of SPARC, a universal regulator of tissue turnover, and in the regulation of macrophage function by stabilin-1-mediated endocytosis.
the role of stabilin-2 and other scavenger receptors in the control of macrophage function, and the role of stabilins in the control of tissue homeostasis.
understanding of the role of SRs and stabilin-1 in particular in the control of inflammatory reactions, tissue homeostatis and immune tolerance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stabilin-1 represents the first SR that couples endocytosis, lysosomal secretion and transcytosis in macrophages.
the endocytic clearance in macrophages is not only a mechanism of disposal of unwanted material but also a means of regulation of the secretory repertoire.
stabilin-1 functions as the endocytic regulator of lysosomal secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stabilin-1 acts as an endocytic receptor that regulates the secretory activity of macrophages by the control of the sorting and transcytosis of stabilin- 1-interacting cargo proteins.
the endocytic clearance can affect the regulated secretion in macrophage and that the endocytosis can be used for delivery of cargo to the secretory pathway.
stabilin-1 acts like a "traffic cop" that controls both endocytic uptake and regulated secretion in macrophage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endocytosis is not just about clearance of unwanted material, it is also about secretion.
macrophages, which are key players of the innate immune system, can be regulated by endocytic clearance of specific ligands and that this process is linked to secretion of soluble mediators.
endocytosis is a key regulatory step for the secretory activity of macrophages and that endosomal sorting of cargo molecules is an important mechanism for the control of macrophage activation.
